review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also checked the upstream definitions it uses: RealInterval, finiteShiftGridAddress, finiteOneShiftFamily, finiteThreeShiftFamily and completeFiniteShiftGridTree. The definitions in this file are finiteShiftGridRootAddress (integer division by 2^depth), finiteShiftGridRootAddresses (an image Finset), completeFiniteShiftGridForest (a biUnion of trees), finiteOneShiftMultiscaleAddresses and finiteOneShiftMultiscaleFamily. All of them are thin compositions of Finset.image, Finset.biUnion and Finset.filter over project-specific grid objects, and none has a Mathlib counterpart. The RealInterval structure that could compete with Mathlib's interval types is defined in FiniteSparseMaximal.lean, not in the target file, so it is outside this review. I found no independent duplicate of an existing Mathlib concept. The theorems are standalone lemmas, which the rubric excludes. I am fairly confident in this result.
